newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan private machinery orders on rising trend - EPA.
newsitem.headline: Japan private machinery orders on rising trend - EPA.

text.p: Japan's private machinery orders are still on a rising trend, an official at the Economic Planning Agency (EPA) said on Monday.

The official said that the expected quarter-on-quarter drop of 8.5 percent for private machinery orders, excluding those for machinery at electric power firms and for ships, in the January-March quarter was a reaction to a 15.3 percent rise in the October-December quarter.
The October-December increase was the highest since April 1987, when the EPA began compiling machinery orders statistics by its present methods, the official said.

On the expected fall for January-March, he also said that as machinery orders had been firm for most of the year, the number of orders before the end of the fiscal year in April was not expected to be as high as usual.

In addition, he said some firms had become more cautious about the economy and while this could also be reflected in the fall seen for the January-March period, it was particularly difficult to make predictions about the April-June quarter.
"We don't know how to look at the April-June quarter," he said.

The 12.8 percent fall in private machinery orders in December from the previous month was a continuing reaction to a 44.2 percent rise in October, he said. Private machinery orders fell in November by 9.7 percent.

In 1996, private machinery orders rose 12.2 percent, climbing for the third year in a row due to strong orders from the car, printing, computer, semiconductor and telecommunication industries, he said.
